title: Raina Sees Dhoni-Yuvraj Quality in Tilak Varma After Record Christchurch Chase
excerpt: Suresh Raina compared Tilak Varma to MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh after Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy chased 68 off the last five overs to beat New Zealand and take a 2-0 series lead.
body:
• Suresh Raina compared Tilak Varma's middle-order temperament to MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh after Varma's unbeaten stand with Nitish Kumar Reddy won the second T20I against New Zealand in Christchurch.
  • India needed 68 runs off the last five overs chasing 181; Varma and Reddy's unbroken 69 off 30 balls got them home with one ball to spare — India's biggest successful chase in the final five overs of a T20I.
  • The win gave India a 2-0 lead in the five-match series, with the third T20I in Wellington on October 27.
  • Raina also praised Reddy's fearless batting, Bhuvneshwar Kumar's comeback and Shreyas Iyer's captaincy.

Suresh Raina does not hand out the comparison lightly — he batted alongside both men for a decade. After Tilak Varma steered India home in a record chase against New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday, the former India batter told ANI that the young left-hander carries the same middle-order quality that defined MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh, according to NDTV Sports.

"When Yuvi Pa, Dhoni bhai and I used to bat at No. 5, 6, 7 and 8, we had a certain passion, and I feel Tilak has that same quality. He is a player with a different mindset and has done exceptionally well. He is contributing with the ball too."

— Suresh Raina, former India batter, to ANI

The chase that prompted it

India were chasing 181 in the second T20I and, with five overs left, still needed 68 runs. Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy stayed unbeaten and added 69 runs in 30 balls, closing out the win with one ball to spare. The 68 runs scored in the final five overs are the most India have ever chased down in that phase of a T20I, surpassing the 60 they scored against Pakistan at the Melbourne Cricket Ground during the 2022 T20 World Cup, when Virat Kohli's unbeaten 82 decided the match, ANI reported via NewKerala.

Raina reserved praise for Reddy as well, noting his fearless, positive batting in the closing overs, and welcomed the comeback of veteran seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar. He also lauded captain Shreyas Iyer, saying Iyer is building a distinct legacy in the format.

Why the comparison carries weight

Dhoni and Yuvraj built their reputations in exactly the position Varma now occupies: the middle overs and the death, where a chase is read ball by ball and panic is the opponent's best bowler. Raina's point was not about technique but temperament — the "certain passion" and "different mindset" he remembered from batting at numbers five through eight with the two senior men. That Varma also contributes overs with the ball strengthens the parallel with Yuvraj, whose left-arm spin was a genuine second skill in India's white-ball sides.

The win put India 2-0 up in the five-match series. The third T20I is in Wellington on October 27, where Varma's finishing will be tested again — this time with every New Zealand analyst in the building having watched the Christchurch tape.

For India's coaching staff, the Christchurch finish also answers a selection question. With the middle order in transition since the Dhoni-Yuvraj era ended, the side has cycled through finishers without settling on one who can also bowl. Varma's unbeaten hand under pressure, paired with Reddy's hitting at the other end, gives India a left-right pair that can be held back for the final overs — the exact role Raina was describing from his own years in the engine room of the chase.
